what: The heuristic identifies customer visited/location facts and the depot from semantic fact names, then reconstructs direct, via-depot, and return routing costs from grounded operator names and metric operator costs. At evaluation it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes a relaxed MST over the current endpoint, remaining customers, and depot, and also computes a nearest-neighbour completion ending at the depot. When exact load, capacity, and all demand PNEs survive translation, the greedy completion respects capacity by selecting direct or via-depot transitions and updating its simulated load; otherwise it safely uses a resource-relaxed transition cost. The final estimate is 75% greedy completion plus 25% MST, with an exact return cost when only the depot goal remains.
why: CVRP states are characterized by a single route endpoint, a monotone unvisited set, possible capacity-triggered depot transitions, and a mandatory final return. Grounded operators expose all relevant routing costs even when numeric travel functions are folded by translation. A greedy completion gives strong state-specific guidance about which nearby customer should be served next, while the MST term captures the global spatial extent of all remaining customers and reduces nearest-neighbour myopia. The optional capacity simulation improves estimates on translations retaining resource constants, while the routing estimate remains fully available when capacity and demand names are absent.
